# 0001: The Projects grid is generated by the macros plugin

Status: accepted (2026-10-22)

## Context

Ticket 06 needs the Projects index to show every project as a card without anyone
editing the index. Zensical's grid cards are plain Markdown (a `<div class="grid cards"
markdown>` around a list) and Zensical has no built-in way to list the pages in a folder.
The `macros` plugin (supported since Zensical 0.0.40; checked against the docs at
`zensical/docs` commit `99f657d`, and built with the pinned 0.0.71) can run Python while
a page renders, but its page context is limited: `navigation` and `files` are empty, so a
macro cannot ask Zensical for the other pages.

## Decision

Use the `macros` plugin with a local `main.py`. Its macros in `tools/project_cards.py`
read the front matter of `content/projects/*.md` from disk and return the card grid
(`project_cards()`) or a project's repo and demo links (`project_links()`).

Jinja is limited to the Projects pages (`render_by_default = false`, `force_render_paths
= "projects/*.md"`), so `{{ ... }}` in a post or the CV is never evaluated.

## Consequences

- Adding a project is one Markdown file. The index, its card and the source check follow.
- The build now runs Python from this repo. Zensical still builds the site, but a
  mistake in `tools/project_cards.py` can break the build (`on_error_fail = true` makes it
  fail loudly instead of printing an error into the page).
- The macro reads files directly, so it depends on the folder layout (`projects/` under
  `docs_dir`), not on Zensical internals. A Zensical upgrade that changed the macro
  environment would show up in the built-site tests.
- Alternative not taken: a script that writes the index file into git. It needs no
  plugin, but the committed index can go stale between runs.
- Cards are sorted by file name. Ordering by `featured` or by date can be added in the
  macro when the custom homepage needs it; today nothing reads `featured`.
